gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-suse: Red Hat Display draws every line like a marker, with daylight showing inside each curve. And SUSE meets it with rounded, friendly forms, so the headline's boldness feels welcoming rather than stern.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-suse-mono: Red Hat Display holds one marker-like line with no hairlines anywhere in the alphabet. SUSE Mono follows with open curves and generous room around each letter, so the two fit together without crowding.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tajawal: Clean, bold, and unfussy from the first word. Flat, unmodulated lines up top meet Tajawal's broad open hook of a c below, and that shared plainness is what holds the sans-serif pairing together.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tasa-explorer: Approachable and bold at once, Red Hat Display keeps its lines plain and constant in width. But TASA Explorer adds a softer note, its curve ends stopping like brush strokes lifted early.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tasa-orbiter: TASA Orbiter reads as a plain sans with small counters that never clog, even when the text gets tiny. Red Hat Display fits above it nicely when given extra size.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-telex: Marker-bold up top, loose and curvy below. Red Hat Display's arches match the thickness of its stems, while Telex has curves that feel unclamped, and that gap between them is the whole appeal.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tenor-sans: Red Hat Display looks cut from one gauge of tubing, stems and curves alike. Tenor Sans adds light but visible thinning at the sides of its bowls, which gives the page a gentle bit of texture.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tirra: Red Hat Display keeps its lines constant, with no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye, and Tirra echoes that with round forms like open parentheses. They sit quietly together.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-titillium-web: Contemporary through and through, Red Hat Display bends its unvarying line like cable into shapes. Titillium Web follows with stroke ends set far apart, giving the text a lighter, more open texture beneath.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tomorrow: Tomorrow reads clean, with bowls that open like a cupped palm of clay. Red Hat Display, with its pencil-line consistency, earns its keep when it runs big and short.
